clue.text: Recent medical graduates bury partners

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Overworked junior doctors are told to bury their partners, a grim picture of hospital life.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a pair against East and West, so 'partners' can be N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Interns are newly qualified doctors serving a supervised hospital year, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: So disgusting that no one takes part

definitions.note: the clue's 'so' just intensifies the adjective

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
some is a part or portion of a whole

explanation.surface: An activity is so repellent that nobody wants to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No one takes part' reads as a single phrase about participation, but it splits into three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome describes something offensive, foul-smelling or nauseating, a close synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: A little sister I called Heather

indicators.note: only a small portion of the following words is wanted, a run of letters tucked inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone recalls naming their younger sister Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a girl's name, matching the sister; it is the plant, and Erica is its botanical genus as well as a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, low evergreen moorland shrubs.

clue.text: Novelist's name on a new book — Vladimir's first

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for name

indicators.note: a new version of a word is a remade one, so its letters are set out afresh

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the given name is needed here

parts.note: the initial of the name Vladimir

explanation.surface: A writer's name appears on a freshly published book, with Vladimir's initial up front.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Vladimir is the novelist's own first name, though here it only supplies its first letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Nabokov was the Russian-American author of Lolita and Pale Fire.

clue.text: Setter seen in Florida

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the pseudonym of the compiler of this very puzzle
second meaning: a large city in central Florida, home of theme parks

explanation.surface: The puzzle's compiler has been spotted on holiday in the Sunshine State.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is referring to himself: Orlando is the pen name on this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando is this puzzle's compiler's pseudonym and also the Florida city famous for Disney World.

clue.text: Rules broken by singer

indicators.note: something broken has its parts smashed apart, ready to be put back in another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Regulations are flouted by a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rules' reads as a plural noun, but it is the verb: a monarch rules or reigns.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold sovereign power, so a monarch who reigns governs the realm.

clue.text: Plentiful ill-gotten gain both sides of border

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are split to sit on either side of the next word, flanking it
something ill-gotten is obtained crookedly, suggesting letters twisted out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged and split
a bound is a limit or boundary line

explanation.surface: Smugglers rake in plenty of dishonest profit on either side of a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Abounding means existing in large quantities, so it is a synonym of plentiful.

clue.text: Erased document about lease

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps itself round the other

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: A legal paper concerning a tenancy has been wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Deleted means removed or struck out from a text or file, the same as erased.

clue.text: Flower Power and criminal reform

indicators.note: to reform is literally to form again, building a new shape from the same letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A campaign slogan, like flower power, calling for penal reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower power was the 1960s hippie slogan, which hides the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown imperial is a tall fritillary with a ring of hanging orange bells, a garden bulb plant.

clue.text: Soprano role — 1,001 duets

wordplay.note: 1,001 in Roman numerals is M plus I, and a duet makes two of it

explanation.surface: An opera singer's part involves a thousand and one duets.
explanation.walkthrough: M is 1,000 and I is 1, so 1,001 is MI; 'duets' asks for it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimì is the consumptive seamstress heroine of Puccini's La Bohème, sung by a soprano.

clue.text: Conductor excluding writer with bad return

parts.note: bar can mean except or excluding, as in 'bar none'
a Biro is a ballpoint pen, the everyday British name

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A conductor is sacked from an orchestra, leaving out a writer whose comeback flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: A Biro is the British word for any ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Barbirolli was a celebrated British conductor, long associated with Manchester's Hallé Orchestra.

clue.text: Return for support after game

indicators.note: after places the support word behind the game word in the final order

parts.note: Go is the ancient Asian board game played with stones
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A player comes back to the team to offer support after the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back is to return to a former place or state, the phrasal verb equivalent.

clue.text: They are wound and screwy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fasteners with two flat flanges, turned by hand onto a bolt

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for crazy people, not an adjective
definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for eccentric or crackpot people

explanation.surface: Some people are wound up tight and a bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury but rhymes with 'round': these things are twisted on by hand. 'Screwy' doubles the hardware joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfly-shaped fasteners are twisted on by finger and thumb, and in slang the term means eccentric extremists.

clue.text: River rose exceptionally, giving rise to water supply

indicators.note: something done exceptionally is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river in flood rose unusually high, feeding the town's water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River rose' reads as a flood report, but both words are simply raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reservoir is a lake, often man-made, where water is stored for public supply.

clue.text: Unnecessary oath from former president I've allowed in

definitions.note: an expletive is both a swear word and, in grammar, a filler word adding nothing to sense

indicators.note: in says the allowed word is placed inside the other letters rather than beside them

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
P is the abbreviation for president
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A former president lets slip a gratuitous swear word, admitting it.
explanation.walkthrough: The allowed piece goes in between the first two pieces and the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is called an expletive, and the grammar term means a word that merely fills a sentence.

clue.text: Frightened of the weather forecast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for nervous or scared
second meaning: describing gusty, blowy conditions a forecaster might predict

explanation.walkthrough: Windy is informal British English for nervous or scared, as in 'getting windy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means jittery in British slang and describes blustery weather with strong breezes.

clue.text: Brushed round seats and tabletop

indicators.note: turning something round sends it back the other way, so the seats word runs backwards

parts.note: pews are the bench seats in a church
the top of table, read as its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone tidying a church hall brushed around the seating and the table surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tabletop' looks like one word for a surface, but it splits into a word and its top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Swept is the past tense of sweep, cleaning with a broom, so it matches brushed.

clue.text: Court poet not quite an insect

indicators.note: not quite all of the poet is used, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A royal court poet is almost, but not quite, a creepy-crawly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a royal household, but it is the verb meaning to pursue romantically.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood ant is a large red forest ant that builds mound nests of pine needles.

clue.text: A spaniel without one is more resilient

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the dog surrounds the one

parts.note: a springer is a breed of spaniel
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spaniel without a companion turns out to be tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, which would remove letters; here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Springier is the comparative of springy, bouncing back readily, so more resilient.

clue.text: Operative like a policeman

definitions.meaning: first meaning: currently valid and having effect, as a law

definitions.note: a cryptic reading: someone serving in the Force
definitions.meaning: second meaning: belonging to the Force, the police service

explanation.walkthrough: 'Operative' looks like a noun for an agent or detective, fitting the policeman, but it is the adjective for a rule in effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulation that is operative is valid and being applied, and an officer serves within the police Force.

clue.text: Going over a river stops bears

indicators.note: going over something means passing across it on both sides, so the stops word straddles the river

parts.note: ends can mean stops or finishes
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A trek across a river is halted by bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animals blocking the way; it is the verb meaning tolerates, and stands last as the definition. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure something is to put up with it, so endures is a synonym of bears or tolerates.

clue.text: Execution may be sedate, we hear

definitions.note: a fill-in: the answer completes the phrase

indicators.note: we hear points to what the word sounds like spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: staid means sedate or prim and respectable

explanation.surface: An execution may be carried out calmly, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sedate' reads as the verb to drug a prisoner, but it is the adjective meaning staid.
explanation.definitionFit: An execution that is stayed is postponed by legal order, the classic use of the verb.

clue.text: One working with trees, working for trees

indicators.note: letters that are working are in motion, not fixed, so they can be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A woodsman is busy on behalf of the trees in their care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' and 'trees' appear twice: first in the plain-sense definition, then as the anagram signal and its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A forester manages woodland, planting and felling timber as a profession.

clue.text: Pals have no right to be devils

indicators.note: having no right means the abbreviation for right is taken away

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Your mates have no business acting like demons.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the standard abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiends are evil spirits or demons, a close synonym of devils.

clue.text: Demand payment? Just so!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to insist on and obtain something owed
second meaning: precise, correct in every detail

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just so!' sounds like agreement, a reply to the question; the punctuation dresses up two plain meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact a fee is to demand it, and something precise and correct is exact.

clue.text: Novel found just behind a kind of dressing-table

indicators.note: behind places the just word after the furniture word in the final order

parts.note: a vanity is a dressing table with a mirror
fair means just or even-handed

explanation.surface: A novel is discovered lying just behind a bedroom dressing table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just behind' reads as 'right behind'; 'just' is its own piece meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity Fair is William Makepeace Thackeray's satirical novel featuring Becky Sharp.

clue.text: Talk openly about East Yorkshire river

parts.note: to air a matter is to discuss it in public
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone discusses frankly a river in East Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Yorkshire' looks like a county name, but East is a separate piece. The Aire flows through Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aire is a river in Yorkshire, northern England, running through Leeds to join the Ouse.

clue.text: Is present given when nurse is enrolled in wartime service?

indicators.note: someone enrolled in a service is placed inside it, so one word goes within another

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, the British women's army branch in the Second World War
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A nurse joining up in wartime raises the question of who is present.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS was the British women's army corps of World War II.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be there at an event, so attends means is present.

clue.text: A tree, when shaken, tinkles

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree with chimes in its branches jingles when the wind shakes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lentisk is the mastic tree, a Mediterranean evergreen shrub yielding aromatic resin.
